---
title: "Combining group descriptives: worked example"
format: html
---

## The problem

Many studies report age (or any continuous baseline variable) only per group,
e.g. treatment vs control. For extraction we often need the whole-sample
N, mean and SD.

The mean is the n-weighted average. The SD is **not** the average of the SDs:
the combined SD must also include the variability *between* group means.

$$
M = \frac{\sum n_i m_i}{N}, \qquad
SD = \sqrt{\frac{\sum \left[(n_i - 1) SD_i^2 + n_i (m_i - M)^2\right]}{N - 1}}
$$

## Load the function

```{r}
source("combine_groups.R")
```

## Example: a two-arm trial

| Group     | n  | Mean age | SD  |
|-----------|----|----------|-----|
| Treatment | 25 | 64.2     | 8.1 |
| Control   | 23 | 66.8     | 7.4 |

```{r}
combine_groups(n = c(25, 23), m = c(64.2, 66.8), sd = c(8.1, 7.4))
```

## Example: three groups

```{r}
combine_groups(n = c(30, 28, 31), m = c(70.1, 68.4, 72.0), sd = c(6.2, 7.0, 5.8))
```

## Example: Amiri 2023

```{r}
amiri2023 <- combine_groups(n = c(25, 25), m = c(54.4, 53.08), sd = c(12.30, 9.31))
amiri2023
```
